purpose: One golden set of .wcs headers with the exact parse each implementation produces, consumed by BOTH packages/skotiq_core/test/services/wcs_conformance_test.dart and the wcs_conformance tests in native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/platesolve.rs, so the two .wcs parsers cannot drift apart silently.

tolerances.verbatim_fields: ra, dec, cd1_1..cd2_2 and every SIP coefficient are read straight out of the card, so they are compared for EXACT equality.
tolerances.derived_fields: pixel_scale, rotation, field_width, field_height are computed, so they are compared to within 1e-9 absolute.

cases.why: A real ASTAP .wcs is fixed-width 80-character cards packed end to end with NO line terminators. Splitting on newlines yields one enormous line, so only SIMPLE is inspected and CRVAL1 is invisible: the solve succeeds and the parse reports it missing. This is the C1 regression, on both sides at once.
cases.divergence: rotation: the Dart parser returns CROTA2 verbatim (+1.25); the Rust parser derives it from the CD matrix as atan2(CD2_1, -CD1_1) (-1.25). The golden header builds CD from CDELT/CROTA2 with the standard AIPS relation (CD1_1=CDELT1*cos, CD1_2=-CDELT2*sin, CD2_1=CDELT1*sin, CD2_2=CDELT2*cos), under which the two are exact negations. Which sign a real ASTAP .wcs implies is NOT verifiable from this repo, so both are pinned as-is and neither parser is changed. Anyone touching either sign convention gets a red build here and must settle it against a real solver output.

cases.why: The same header written one padded card per line with CRLF terminators. Must parse to byte-identical results as astap_card_stream: the card splitter honours newlines first and only splits segments longer than one card.
cases.divergence: rotation: the Dart parser returns CROTA2 verbatim (+1.25); the Rust parser derives it from the CD matrix as atan2(CD2_1, -CD1_1) (-1.25). The golden header builds CD from CDELT/CROTA2 with the standard AIPS relation (CD1_1=CDELT1*cos, CD1_2=-CDELT2*sin, CD2_1=CDELT1*sin, CD2_2=CDELT2*cos), under which the two are exact negations. Which sign a real ASTAP .wcs implies is NOT verifiable from this repo, so both are pinned as-is and neither parser is changed. Anyone touching either sign convention gets a red build here and must settle it against a real solver output.

cases.why: astrometry.net writes IMAGEW/IMAGEH instead of NAXIS1/2, a CD matrix with exact-zero off-diagonal terms (north-up, rotation 0), SIP distortion terms and the A_DMAX diagnostic sibling that must NOT be read as a polynomial term. No CDELT and no CROTA2 anywhere.
cases.divergence: pixel scale and rotation: the Dart parser reads only CDELT1/CROTA2 and this header has neither, so it reports pixel_scale 0 and rotation 0 while still reporting success on CRVAL1/CRVAL2. The Rust parser derives both from the CD matrix. The Dart parser also ignores the CD matrix and every SIP term entirely: its PlateSolveResult leaves cd11..cd22 and the SIP vectors unset by design (pinned by plate_solve_service_test.dart 'a local-parser success carries position but no CD/SIP').

cases.why: A solved header that carries CDELT/CROTA but no CD matrix. This is the sharpest divergence between the two parsers and the reason this fixture exists.
cases.divergence: SUCCESS vs ERROR on the same solved header. Dart requires only CRVAL1/CRVAL2 and derives scale/rotation from CDELT1/CROTA2; Rust additionally requires all four CD terms and fails with WcsMissingKeyword{CD1_1} when they are absent. Neither is changed here: the Rust path feeds SipWcs, which cannot be built without a CD matrix, while the Dart path only needs RA/Dec for centering. Recorded, not unified.

cases.why: Cards whose '=' sits at column 7 instead of the FITS-mandated column 8 (keyword not padded to 8). Pins how strictly each parser reads the card layout.
cases.divergence: Rust reads the keyword from columns 0..8 and requires '=' at column 8, so every card here is skipped and the parse fails on the first required keyword. Dart matches with startsWith() and splits on the first '=', so it accepts the off-standard layout. Rust is the standard-conformant reader; Dart is the lenient one. Recorded, not unified — tightening Dart could reject headers it reads today.

cases.why: A malformed CRVAL1 must never become a 'successful' solve at RA 0. Both parsers must fail closed; they report the failure differently.
cases.divergence: Both fail closed, with different diagnostics: Rust names the keyword and the raw value (WcsParse), Dart returns the generic 'Could not parse WCS file' because an unparseable value is indistinguishable from an absent one in its Optional-based accumulation.

cases.why: Half a position is not a position. Missing CRVAL2 must fail on both sides rather than yielding Dec 0.
A sidecar with no WCS keywords at all — the shape a failed solve leaves behind.

Edge case the fixture exists to document rather than to bless: the literal 'NaN' is accepted by Rust f64::from_str AND by Dart double.tryParse, so a WCS carrying it produces a solve both parsers report as SUCCESSFUL with a NaN position. Pinned as current behaviour on both sides; see README 'Known hazards'.

at.0: CRVAL1  = NaN / hazard: parses as a float in BOTH languages

cases.divergence: Agreement, but on a hazard: both sides report success with a NaN RA. Nothing downstream of either parser rejects NaN. Not changed in this pass (a fix is a behaviour change and needs a reproduction in the running app), but pinned so the hazard cannot be forgotten and so a future guard has to update BOTH sides at once.
